included_preprints.family_title: The irrationality exponent of π is 2.
included_preprints.title: The irrationality exponent of pi is 2
included_preprints.abstract: We prove the conjecture that the irrationality exponent of π is 2. As a consequence, the classical Flint–Hills series $`\sum_{n\ge1}1/(n^3\sin^2 n)`$ converges, with angles in radians.
included_preprints.abstract_upstream_markup: We prove the conjecture that the irrationality exponent of π is 2. As a consequence, the classical Flint–Hills series $`\sum_{n\ge1}1/(n^3\sin^2 n)`$ converges, with angles in radians.
included_preprints.family_claim_description: Proves that the irrationality exponent of π is exactly 2: for every ε > 0 and all sufficiently large denominators q, every rational $`p/q`$ satisfies $`|\pi-p/q|\ge q^{-2-\varepsilon}`$. This also proves convergence of the Flint–Hills series $`\sum_{n\ge1}1/(n^3\sin^2 n)`$, with angles in radians. ([Lean](lean/docs/017.md))
